# dsh-restart
English | 中文
A **Restart** page in the DeepSeek Harness (dsh) Web settings panel: one button replaces the running
host process with a fresh one.
## What it does
- **Host half** registers three routes on the Web server, all limited to direct same-origin loopback

requests:
- `GET /dsh-restart/status` — boot id, PID, start time, and serving port of the current p

rocess
- `POST /dsh-restart/restart` — replaces the current process (the host exits after answering

`202`)
- `POST /dsh-restart/stop` — ends the current process and starts nothing (same ordering)
- **
Browser half** registers a `settings.section` page showing that identity, a restart button, and a st

op button.
- **Shortcut** — Cmd+Shift+K (macOS) or Ctrl+Shift+K (Windows) restarts the host without
opening settings. Rebind it on the settings *Keyboard* page like any other command. It fires from th
e page and from editable surfaces such as the composer, while terminal input keeps it out, and it ap
pears with its label on the settings *Keyboard* page. Web on Linux is left unbound: the client's sho
rtcut allowlist rejects every `primary+alt` chord there, so registering one would fail the plugin's
activation. After a restart it polls `/dsh-restart/status` and reloads the page as soon as a differe
nt boot id answers; after a stop there is nothing to wait for, so the page reports success once the
status route stops answering — and says plainly that starting again means running the launch command
ops answering — and says plainly that starting again means running the launch command in a terminal.
The restart itself is done by a detached helper: the host exits after 400 ms, and the helper waits u
ntil the port stops accepting connections before spawning the replacement with **exactly the same la
unch invocation** (Node binary, `execArgv`, absolute entry path, remaining argv, working directory).
That ordering is what keeps the replacement from dying of `EADDRINUSE` while the old socket is stil
l held. Logs land in the system temp directory as `dsh-restart-<timestamp>.out.log` / `.err.log`.
A stop is the same 400 ms `SIGTERM` with no helper behind it, which is what lets the CLI flush sessi
ons and dispose plugins before its own escalation timer forces the exit. Because a stopped host has
no replacement, the process you restart from the page is also the one no longer attached to your ter
minal — after any restart, stopping it means this button, `kill <pid>`, or `curl -X POST http://127.
0.0.1:<port>/dsh-restart/stop`.
Sessions live on disk and survive the restart, and plugins that are installed but not active yet loa
sk and survive the restart, and plugins that are installed but not active yet load on the next boot.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The first install needs one restart before the page exists — restart the host from a terminal, or us
e dshmarket's restart button once. After that, this page is the way to restart.
## Endpoint contract
`POST /dsh-restart/restart` accepts only requests whose peer is loopback and whose `Origin` matches
`Host`; any forwarding header (`Forwarded`, `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Real-IP`) or non-loopback peer is
refused with `403`. It answers `202`, then the host exits and the helper starts the replacement.
`POST /dsh-restart/stop` takes the same guard and answers `202` before exiting, so the browser learn
s the outcome from the response instead of from a dropped connection. It never sends `SIGKILL`: the
graceful signal is what flushes sessions.
## Test
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Covers: the detached helper really starts a replacement process, all four refusal paths of the same-
origin guard, and the client bundle's registration and render. Set `DSH_CHECKOUT=<dsh checkout>` to
add an SSR render assertion using that checkout's React; without it that one assertion is skipped.
